messages:
Noah: heads-up — seeing a ~35% jump in TTFT for route /v1/complete-text starting ~09:12 UTC. p50 moved 220ms -> 300ms. no traffic spike. anyone on call?
Maria: on it. linking traces, can you drop a trace id?
Noah: trace 0a4f9c3b. quick metric snapshot: `ttft_p50 220->300ms`, `kernel_exec_p50 90->150ms`, queue_wait stable. looks like kernel heavy.
Sam: pulling perf traces now. running flamegraphs from the probe. early view shows kernel time taking a bigger slice and kv lookup tail rising for some hosts.
Sam: sample flamegraph notes: "kernel_exec 58% | kv_lookup 18% | queue_wait 12% | postproc 12%" (worker-52, n=120)
Raj: any recent changes to batcher heuristics or kernel selector? we rolled a scheduler change overnight.
Liz: yeah, runtime-scheduler commit abcdef1 toggled microbatch target from fixed 16 -> adaptive. under sparse seqs it often targets 4. landed in canary at 08:55.
Maria: adaptive microbatching shrinking batches would increase kernel overhead amortization loss. that fits kernel_exec increase. but why kv lookup tail rise?
Noah: infra-bot shows runtime-scheduler@abcdef1 rolled to 10% in eu-west at 08:55. correlated with the TTFT bump.
perf-bot: ALERT: route=/v1/complete-text ttft_p50 +36% detected 08:55->09:15. Related deploy: runtime-scheduler@abcdef1 rolled to 10% (eu-west).
Sam: per-host microbatch snapshot (09:00-09:20): host-52 mb=4, host-14 mb=4, host-23 mb=12. small batches on 52/14 match slower p50.
Sam: running SQL to split kernel vs kv by host: `SELECT host, avg(ttft) ttft, avg(kernel_ms) kernel FROM token_metrics WHERE route='/v1/complete-text' GROUP BY host ORDER BY ttft DESC LIMIT 10;` results attached to probe.
Raj: suggest pausing the canary and rolling back affected hosts. also we need better token-level panels: prequeue, queue, kernel_exec, kv_lookup, decode_postproc. current dash lumps kernel+kv and hides the pattern.
Liz: I can add a temp grafana panel under eng-runtime/perf/token-breakdown. promql for kernel slice: `rate(token_kernel_time_ms_sum[5m]) / rate(token_count[5m])`. kv similar. will include host filter and p50/p95.
Maria: looked at kernel selector logs — heuristic mis-estimated sequence distribution and routed small sequences to the small-ops kernel for many jobs. small-ops kernel is slower for medium-sized matmuls vs the fast fused path. combined with tiny microbatches it gets worse.
Noah: sounds like two amplifying factors: (1) adaptive microbatch collapse, (2) selector choosing suboptimal kernel. plan: pause canary, rollback eu-west, patch selector heuristic, add dashboard split, run replay probes.
Raj: rolling back now — initiating rollback of runtime-scheduler@abcdef1 -> 0% in eu-west.
infra-bot: Deploy rollback started: runtime-scheduler@abcdef1 -> 0% (eu-west). status: in progress.
Liz: adding the grafana panel now. will push panel JSON and a direct link in this thread.
Maria: I'll write a unit test for selector to catch this degenerate case (sparse seq dist + adaptive microbatch => avoid small-ops kernel). will open PR with fix.
Sam: running replay probe against the canary hosts: `./tools/replay_probe --hosts host-52,host-14 --seq-dist=sparse --samples=200` — reproduces p50 bump. kernel_p50 ~148ms on canary hosts vs ~92ms on control.
Noah: good repro. after rollback please rerun and post numbers.
Sam: post-rollback probe results (09:48): kernel_p50 ~95ms, ttft_p50 back to ~210ms on those hosts. kv tail roughly same. rollback fixed main regression.
Raj: follow-ups: add rollout gating to prevent scheduler canaries from hitting small fraction of high-traffic route hosts without kernel selector quickchecks.
Liz: also adding alert: token_kernel_ms_p50 increase >20% for 10m scoped by route+host. example rule will compare recent kernel ms per-token to baseline variable.
Maria: PR opened for selector fix and unit test. tagging @eng-runtime for review.
Noah: I'll draft a short postmortem doc and link the new dashboard, traces, probe outputs, and commits. assigning owners: Liz dashboard, Maria selector PR, Raj rollout gating, Sam extended probes, Noah postmortem.
Sam: one more ops ask: add host heatmap panel for kernel_p50 by route so we can spot small-fraction regressions.
Liz: noted, will add heatmap and a host-filterable panel.
Noah: thanks all. keeping thread open until PR merged and guarded canary resumed. :white_check_mark:
